subject: Re: Request for closure evidence and production verification — PT finding #7 (auth bypass)
messages:
From: Martin Cole <security@starlitehealth.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request for closure evidence and production verification — PT finding #7 (auth bypass)

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the remediation plan you shared last week. Our external pen test vendor (ZB Consulting) reopened a medium/high item — PT#7 — which described an authentication bypass on a legacy endpoint used by some internal tools.

Before we sign off, the SOC2 auditor has asked for concrete evidence that the fix was deployed to production and that compensating controls are in place while we validate. Specifically could you provide:

- A screenshot of the production dashboard showing the endpoint is returning 403/401 for the prior bad request vector (with timestamp)
- Relevant production config change (nginx or gateway) — redacted keys ok, but include the exact directive lines and change comment
- The ticket(s) that tracked the fix and the deploy job/logs showing the migration to prod
- Any short-term compensating controls (WAF rules, rate limits, anomaly alerts) you put in place while validation is ongoing

We need these items by EOD Aug 3 to include in the auditor packet. If you can surface audit logs for the exact time of change, that would be ideal.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — happy to jump on a 20 min screen share if that helps.

Best,
Martin
Security Lead, Starlite Health
From: camila_reyes@redwood.com
To: Martin Cole <security@starlitehealth.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request for closure evidence and production verification — PT finding #7 (auth bypass)

Martin — thanks for the clear list. We've kicked this up to Ops and Infra and will assemble a consolidated evidence package. High-level timeline:

- Jul 30 02:00 UTC: config change applied to gateway + short WAF rule enabled (temporary)
- Jul 30 02:10 UTC: smoke tests + canary verification passed
- Jul 30 02:20 UTC: full deploy completed to prod pool-03

I'll pull screenshots, the exact config diff (redacted for secrets), the CI/CD deploy job output, and a CSV export of the relevant audit log entries. Vivek will attach the artifacts; Neha will confirm the compensating controls and update the SOC2 tracker.

If you need anything formatted for the auditor (PDF bundle), say the word and we'll prepare it.

—Camila
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com, Martin Cole <security@starlitehealth.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request for closure evidence and production verification — PT finding #7 (auth bypass)

Martin / Camila — attaching the artifacts from the deploy and verification run. Attachment stubs below:

- redwood_auth-fix-screenshot-2026-07-30.png (screenshot from /admin/requests showing 403 for the malformed token)
- nginx-config-auth-block-2026-07-30.txt (snippet: location /legacy/internal { deny all; proxy_pass ... } — keys/redacted)
- JIRA-RED-4523-prod-deploy-log.txt (CI job steps showing promotion to prod, run ids)
- auditlog-20260730-0200UTC.csv (audit entries around the change; shows config change event and user id: infra-deploy-bot)

Summary of compensating controls applied on Jul 30 UTC:
- WAF rule WAF-INT-127 added to block the specific URL pattern used by the test vector (temporary, will be reviewed at end of month)
- Increased anomaly alerting on authentication failure rates for the affected service (threshold lowered from 10/min to 3/min)
- Restrictive ingress ACLs were applied to the internal-only endpoint from ip-subnets used by internal tools

Notes on redaction: we removed internal IPs for PII and redacted API keys. If the auditor requires unredacted logs under an NDA, we can coordinate an SFTP drop.

Let me know if you need expanded log ranges.

—Vivek
Engineering Manager, Infrastructure
From: Martin Cole <security@starlitehealth.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, pen-test@zbconsulting.com
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request for closure evidence and production verification — PT finding #7 (auth bypass)

Thanks Vivek — these look useful. A couple quick asks before we close the finding/mark fixed in our tracker:

1) Can you confirm the exact UTC timestamp when the gateway config (nginx) was changed and which user/service account performed the change? We need this for the auditor to correlate to the deploy job id.
2) We require at least one example of a pre-change request (showing the vulnerable response) and a post-change request (showing the blocked/403 response). You provided the post screenshot; can you provide a sanitized pre-change sample from your test archive?
3) Please include the WAF rule definition (the matching regex or rule id) and the planned removal/retention date for the temporary rule.

ZB Consulting also asked whether the fix is gated behind a feature flag or if it's a permanent config change. That affects their retest strategy.

If you can get these by EOD Tue (Aug 3) we can include them in the auditor packet. Otherwise we'll scope the retest date to Sep 1.

Regards,
Martin
From: camila_reyes@redwood.com
To: Martin Cole <security@starlitehealth.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, pen-test@zbconsulting.com
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2026 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request for closure evidence and production verification — PT finding #7 (auth bypass)

Martin — attaching the follow-ups you requested and a short narrative for the auditor. Attachments (sent): redwood_auth-fix-screenshot-2026-07-30.png, nginx-config-auth-block-2026-07-30.txt, JIRA-RED-4523-prod-deploy-log.txt, auditlog-20260730-0200UTC.csv.

Short narrative (for the auditor):
- UTC timestamp of nginx change: 2026-07-30T02:03:12Z — performed by service account infra-deploy-bot (see auditlog entry id 987654321)
- Pre-change sample: included in Drive bundle as pre-change-request-sample-20260729.txt (sanitized)
- Post-change sample: redwood_auth-fix-screenshot-2026-07-30.png (timestamp visible)
- WAF rule: WAF-INT-127 — rule matches path regex ^/legacy/internal/.*\?token=.* and blocks on payload patterns matching malformed-token-pattern-01. Temporary retention: rule will remain in place until 2026-08-30 for monitoring, then reviewed and either graduated to permanent WAF or removed.
- Scope: this is a permanent config hardening (deny on the legacy endpoint) plus short-term WAF protection; not feature-flagged.

Next steps: I'll package a PDF auditor bundle and drop the link to the Drive folder (shared above) by EOD Aug 4. If ZB needs an expedited retest, we can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough and provide unredacted logs under NDA.

Thanks for the patience — let me know if the auditor needs a signed attestation.

—Camila
